easy.explanation: Ahaz is identified as the son of Jotham.
The KJV says that Ahaz reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem.
easy.q: How many years did Ahaz reign in Jerusalem?

answers: Only at the end of his reign
easy.explanation: The passage says that Ahaz did not do that which was right in the sight of the LORD.
easy.q: Did Ahaz do that which was right in the sight of the LORD?

medium.explanation: The KJV says, “he walked in the way of the kings of Israel.”
medium.q: In whose way did Ahaz walk?

answers: He made his son pass through the fire
He built a wall around Jerusalem
He sent his son to Assyria
medium.explanation: The passage says that Ahaz made his son pass through the fire.
medium.q: What additional wicked practice did Ahaz perform?

medium.explanation: The high places were elevated sites where Ahaz sacrificed and burned incense.
medium.q: What were the “high places” where Ahaz sacrificed?

answers: His actions were according to the abominations of the heathen
His actions were described as the acts of David
challenge.explanation: Making his son pass through the fire is said to be according to the abominations of the heathen.
challenge.q: How does the passage connect Ahaz’s actions with the nations?

answers: Ahaz was favorably compared with David
Ahaz did not follow the approved example of David
challenge.explanation: Ahaz did not do what was right like David his father.
challenge.q: What does the mention of David show about Ahaz’s character?

answers: In the high places, on the hills, and under every green tree
challenge.explanation: Verse 4 lists the high places, the hills, and every green tree.
challenge.q: Where did Ahaz sacrifice and burn incense?

paragraphs.title: The Siege and the Appeal to Assyria

easy.explanation: Rezin king of Syria and Pekah king of Israel came against Jerusalem.
easy.q: Who came up to fight against Jerusalem?

easy.explanation: They besieged Ahaz but could not overcome him.
easy.q: Did Rezin and Pekah conquer Jerusalem?

easy.explanation: Ahaz sent messengers to Tiglath-pileser, king of Assyria.
easy.q: To whom did Ahaz appeal for help?

answers: Silver and gold as a present
medium.explanation: Ahaz took silver and gold from the LORD’s house and the king’s treasures and sent it as a present.
medium.q: What did Ahaz send to the king of Assyria?

answers: Save him from the king of Syria and the king of Israel
medium.explanation: Ahaz asked to be saved from the two kings who were attacking him.
medium.q: What did Ahaz ask the king of Assyria to do?

answers: Damascus was captured and Rezin was killed
medium.explanation: The king of Assyria took Damascus, carried away its people, and slew Rezin.
medium.q: What happened after the king of Assyria responded?

answers: From the house of the LORD and the king’s treasures
From the camp of the king of Israel
challenge.explanation: The passage names the house of the LORD and the treasures of the king’s house.
challenge.q: From where did Ahaz take the silver and gold?

answers: He offered himself as a subordinate ally of the Assyrian king
He claimed to be the Assyrian king’s actual son
He invited the Assyrian king to rule Judah
challenge.explanation: The words express submission and a request for protection from Assyria.
challenge.q: What did Ahaz mean by saying, “I am thy servant and thy son”?

answers: Elath was recovered for Syria, and Syrians dwelt there
challenge.explanation: Rezin recovered Elath to Syria, and the Syrians came to dwell there.
challenge.q: What geographic change happened to Elath?

paragraphs.title: The Altar from Damascus and Ahaz’s Orders

easy.explanation: Ahaz saw an altar that was at Damascus.
easy.q: What did Ahaz see in Damascus?

easy.explanation: Ahaz sent the fashion and pattern of the altar to Urijah the priest.
easy.q: To whom did Ahaz send the design and pattern of the altar?

easy.explanation: Urijah built the altar according to all that Ahaz had sent.
easy.q: Who built the altar in Jerusalem?

answers: He approached it and offered upon it
medium.explanation: The king approached the altar and offered thereon.
medium.q: What did Ahaz do after he came from Damascus and saw the altar?

answers: Use it as the main altar
Keep it for his own use in a secondary role
medium.explanation: Ahaz said that the brasen altar would be for him to enquire by.
medium.q: What did Ahaz command concerning the brasen altar?

answers: A liquid offering poured out on the altar
medium.explanation: Ahaz poured his drink offering upon the altar as part of the sacrifice.
medium.q: What is a “drink offering” in this passage?

answers: Ahaz made the decision and had the priest carry it out
Ahaz gave the kingdom to Urijah
challenge.explanation: Ahaz issued the order, and Urijah built the altar according to it.
challenge.q: What does Ahaz’s sending the design to Urijah show about his rule?

answers: Ahaz saw an altar, sent its pattern, and Urijah built it
Urijah built an altar, and then Ahaz sent the pattern
The Assyrian king built an altar, and Ahaz destroyed it
challenge.explanation: That is the order given in verses 10–11.
challenge.q: Which sequence of events is described?

answers: The morning and evening offerings, the king’s offerings, and the people’s offerings
challenge.explanation: Ahaz commanded that the various offerings and their blood be placed upon the great altar.
challenge.q: What offerings were to be made upon the great altar?

easy.explanation: The KJV says that Ahaz cut off the borders of the bases.
Ahaz took down the sea from off the brasen oxen.
easy.q: From what was the sea removed?

answers: He turned it away from the house of the LORD
easy.explanation: The passage says that he turned the king’s entry without from the house of the LORD.
easy.q: What did Ahaz do to the king’s entry without?

answers: He removed it from the bases
He built an altar for it
medium.explanation: Ahaz removed the laver from off the bases.
medium.q: What did Ahaz do to the laver?

medium.explanation: The sea was placed upon a pavement of stones.
medium.q: Where did Ahaz put the sea after removing it from the brasen oxen?

answers: Because of the king of Assyria
Because of the king of Syria
medium.explanation: The passage says the changes were made for the king of Assyria.
medium.q: Why did Ahaz turn these temple features away?

answers: It connects them with fear or pressure from the king of Assyria
It connects them with victory over Syria
challenge.explanation: The changes are described as being made because of the king of Assyria.
challenge.q: What connection does the passage make between the temple changes and Ahaz’s political situation?

answers: Its location and support were changed
challenge.explanation: The sea was removed from the oxen and placed on a pavement of stones.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from removing the sea from the brasen oxen?

answers: The covert for the sabbath and the king’s entry without
The gate of Damascus and the gate of Elath
The temple gate and the inner palace gate
challenge.explanation: Both the covert for the sabbath and the king’s entry without are mentioned.
challenge.q: Which two entrances or structures were altered?

answers: In the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah
In the records of the kings of Assyria
In the book of the law of Moses
easy.explanation: The passage refers readers to the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah.
easy.q: Where were the rest of Ahaz’s acts written?

easy.explanation: Ahaz was buried with his fathers in the city of David.
Hezekiah, Ahaz’s son, reigned in his stead.

medium.explanation: This is a biblical expression describing Ahaz’s death.
medium.q: What does “Ahaz slept with his fathers” mean?

medium.explanation: The verse says, “Hezekiah his son reigned in his stead.”
medium.q: What was Hezekiah’s relationship to Ahaz?

medium.explanation: Hezekiah reigned in Ahaz’s place after Ahaz died.
medium.q: What does the phrase “in his stead” mean?

answers: It indicates that more details about Ahaz can be found there
It announces that the chapter ends with a war
It says that Hezekiah wrote this chapter
challenge.explanation: The reference directs readers to another record for the rest of Ahaz’s acts.
challenge.q: What is the purpose of the reference to the book of the chronicles?

answers: Ahaz died, was buried in the city of David, and Hezekiah became king
Hezekiah became king, Ahaz died, and Ahaz was buried in Damascus
Ahaz was buried, a war followed, and Pekah became king
challenge.explanation: This is the order presented in verse 20.
challenge.q: Which sequence summarizes the end of the chapter?

answers: The kingship passed from Ahaz to his son
The kingdom of Judah passed to Assyria
challenge.explanation: The verse states that Hezekiah his son reigned in Ahaz’s stead.
challenge.q: What can be concluded from the introduction of Hezekiah at the end?
